orchestkit · #3215 · #3218

The linter reported zero because it could not read the file

#3216 shipped a reachability linter that printed DEAD-EDGE: 0. It was matching only the inline YAML form skills: [a, b]. Every file using the block form returned nothing, and nothing is indistinguishable from clean. That hid five real skill edges and the entire agent surface. A green check that cannot see the defect is worse than no check, because it ends the search.

The two shapes, and why one was invisible

skills use the inline form ...
  skills: [architecture-decision-record, chain-patterns]
          ^ matched

... while all 36 agents and 5 design-* skills use the block form
  skills:
    - accessibility
    - ui-components
    ^ regex returns nothing, linter prints 0, everyone relaxes

Now parsed, not matched. Deliberately dependency-free: js-yaml resolves in this tree today, but it is a transitive package rather than a declared dependency, so a test must not import it.

What the linter checks now

CheckPolicyNow
DEAD-EDGE
skill preload naming a blocked target		 hard zero always a bug, and cheap: something already wants it0
AGENT-DEAD-EDGE
agent preload naming a blocked target		 ratchet 94 clearing it is per-agent judgement, not a sweep94
UNREACHABLE
both flags, invokable by nobody		 ratchet 29 reachability costs session tokens29
MISSING-TARGET
preload naming a skill that does not exist		 hard zero never acceptable0

The ratchets are self-tightening. Give one of the 29 a dependant and DEAD-EDGE fires, forcing the un-flag, which lowers the baseline. The linter also prints the new number when a count falls, so locking in a gain is a one-line edit rather than an archaeology exercise.

The five it had been hiding, now fixed

EdgeFix
design-context-extract, design-import, design-stylecards, design-to-code → design-system-tokens un-flagged the target: four edges for one change, and it also repaired 4 agent edges
design-ship → create-pr deleted the declaration. create-pr is a deliberate user-only mutating action; weakening it would let the model open PRs unprompted

The budget is now the binding constraint

skill index   22466 / 22500 bytes    34 bytes spare
session total  9040 / 9300 tokens

Un-flagging design-system-tokens cost 264 bytes and only fit because its description was trimmed by 72 first. Working the 94 agent edges down cannot proceed by un-flagging: at 34 bytes of headroom, each future target has to pay for itself out of its own description, so deleting the false declaration is the default and un-flagging is the rare exception.
